entries.title: Author lists fold away under an article's title
entries.body: When an article opens, the authors, affiliations and contact lines under its title are folded away, so you start with the article itself; a 'Show authors and details' button under the title brings them back. A line that only repeated the title is hidden as well. The back arrow above the title is gone, since the Spideryarn mark in the bottom bar already takes you to your library.

entries.title: Help is split into a page per topic
entries.body: Help is a contents page leading to a separate page for each topic, each mode and each guide, with new guides for students, reviewers and experts, and one page for common questions. Its search reads the text of every page, old Help links still arrive at the right place, and the Help links in the bottom bar and the command bar open the page for the mode you are in. The Help link is back in the bottom bar for everyone, just before Feedback.

entries.title: Less-used modes move into a More menu
entries.body: Quotes, Glossary, FAQ, Ideas and Timeline sit in a More menu in the bottom bar (FAQ and Timeline need the Experimental features switch); an open one keeps its own button. The first Tab press offers a 'Skip to modes' link, and the rows that switch a mode's views look alike everywhere and scroll sideways on narrow screens.

entries.title: Easier to use by phone and keyboard
entries.body: On a phone, the Metadata and profile pages show their contents list and search box above the page, where before they were missing. Small controls such as passage links and sign-in links get a finger-sized target without changing how they look, and keyboard focus is clearly visible on more controls, including Structure's outline and the notes beside the article.

entries.title: Dictation records for up to fifteen minutes
entries.body: Dictating into a text box can run for up to fifteen minutes. In the last minute a countdown and a warning chime tell you it is about to stop, and another chime marks the stop itself. A Feedback report can hold up to 20,000 characters, so a long dictated report fits.

entries.title: Referee shows hidden text in its own view
entries.body: Referee's check for hidden instructions in a paper moves out of the Notices box into its own Hidden text view, which explains each trick in plain words and groups repeated findings with a count. Adding a criterion no longer quietly deletes your oldest one: a list holds up to 200, and adding past that is refused with a sentence.

entries.title: Fixes to adding an article, and to Stop
entries.body: Pressing Stop as an article finished adding could lose it; it is now kept. An article that hit a problem while being added no longer sits stuck, the progress card shows its title, and PDFs are less likely to be interrupted. Pasting a Spideryarn reading-page link into Add asks you to open that page or give the original address.

entries.title: Comment edits, Japanese typing and library search fixed
entries.body: Changing a comment while the AI's answer to it was still appearing could undo the change; it no longer does. When typing Japanese or Chinese, the Enter or Escape that picks a suggested word could send, save or close something; it no longer does. On your library page, a chosen topic or tag also narrows the passages a search finds.
